mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rebound after the sharp t-0w drop, commuting footfall returns to city-center shops and lifts RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace and transit mobility stay depressed while retail still rises.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w WORKPLACES=-1.7 and TRANSIT=-2.0 after prior positive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise back above their t-1w levels for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold break in TRANSIT below zero signals a strong demand shock and reduces access to retail precincts, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next one to two weeks. The effect fails if transit falls but retail does not weaken immediately.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 0 after being positive in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from 11.4 at t-1w to -2.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or abrupt access shock
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after TRANSIT crosses from positive to negative.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility turns positive while WORKPLACES fall, people substitute local errands and avoid discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The signal fails if home-centered behavior rises without any retail pullback.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased to 2.0 at t-0w while WORKPLACES fell to -1.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior 4-week mean when RESIDENTIAL is above 0 and WORKPLACES is below 0 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM reflects bundled essential trips that crowd out discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks after grocery mobility jumps. The hypothesis fails if grocery visits rise but retail does not weaken shortly afterward.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 11.0 at t-1w to 18.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after a grocery/pharmacy surge of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS use marks favorable weather and outdoor activity, which draws time away from indoor retail and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following month. The mechanism fails if park mobility rises but retail also rises.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased from 0.6 at t-1w to 8.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not below its previous 4-week average after a sustained PARKS increase lasting at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both drop while RESIDENTIAL rises, households substitute away from trip-chaining and discretionary shopping, creating a short-run fall in RETAIL_REC within one week. The claim fails if the co-movement does not produce an immediate retail drop.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move down in the week after simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside a positive RESIDENTIAL reading.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction regime, a negative TRANSIT reading combined with negative WORKPLACES indicates mobility suppression that depresses retail demand for up to four weeks. Outside restriction periods, the same transit/workplace pattern has little predictive value.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below 0 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES turn negative.

mechanism_narrative: A quick rebound in GROCERY_PHARM followed by weak PARKS activity indicates consumers are substituting toward errands rather than leisure, which supports RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as shopping consolidates near home. The hypothesis fails if grocery strength is not followed by retail improvement.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM=18.4 at t-0w while PARKS=8.1 after 0.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 4-week mean within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated and PARKS does not continue to accelerate.
